**Finding: Compliant** — no redline required.

The agreement contains no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binding Bluefly:

- **§ 14.16 (Freedom of Action)** affirmatively states "Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others," which directly preserves our right to buy hosting and related services from other suppliers.
- The only uses of "exclusive"/"nonexclusive" are the warranty disclaimer heading (§ 5.2) and license grants running in our favour (§§ 5.4, 12.1) — neither is a restrictive covenant.
- The planner's flagged sections check out clean: **§ 13.1 (Services)** deals only with IBM's change rights and our termination right, and **§ 11.5 (Capacity Planning)** allocates capacity-planning responsibility without any single-source requirement.
- **§ 14.11 (No Resale)** bars us from reselling the Services but does not restrict our procurement from third parties, so it is outside the scope of this rule.
- No minimum-purchase or "all of its requirements" commitment appears anywhere in the document.

This satisfies the preferred position (no exclusivity on Customer), so the fallback (category-limited, 12-month exclusivity with performance exit) is not needed.
